svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.10 FIRE PROTECTION
Area and Location of Exposing Building Face

g.text: Area of the exposing building face
one direction, from finished ground level to the
uppermost ceiling, the gable above is not counted

Plan of a stepped wall, cut low

Irregular or skewed wall: where the face is taken (plan)

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
The area of an exposing building face is taken as the exterior wall area
facing in one direction on any side of a building
Calculated as (i) the total area measured from the finished ground level to the
uppermost ceiling, or (ii) the area for each fire compartment, where a building
is divided into fire compartments by fire separations with fire-resistance
ratings not less than 45 min. Except as permitted by Sentence (4).
For Table 9.10.14.4.-A and an irregularly shaped or skewed exterior wall,
the exposing building face is a vertical plane with no unprotected
openings between it and the line to which the limiting distance is
measured
This plane sets the maximum aggregate area of unprotected openings. See Note
For Table 9.10.14.5.-A and an irregularly shaped or skewed exterior wall
(a) the exposing building face is a vertical plane with no portion of the actual
exposing building face between it and the line to which the limiting distance is
measured, for the type of construction, cladding and fire-resistance rating, and
(b) the maximum area of unprotected openings in the second column of that Table
is determined with the limiting distance measured from that plane. See Note
Where a building is divided by fire separations into fire compartments,
the area of exposing building face is permitted to be calculated for each
fire compartment
Provided the fire separations have a fire-resistance rating not less than 45
min.
Definitions (Division A)
Exposing building face: the part of the exterior wall of a building that faces
one direction and is located between ground level and the ceiling of its top
storey or, where a building is divided into fire compartments, the exterior wall
of a fire compartment that faces one direction. Limiting distance: the distance
from an exposing building face to a property line, the centre line of a street,
lane or public thoroughfare, or an imaginary line between 2 buildings or fire
compartments on the same property, measured at right angles to the exposing
building face.
The construction plane is used first. The percentage of unprotected openings it
gives would be unnecessarily restrictive where the actual openings are in a
plane set back from the front of the face.
Drawn: in A and B red is the face area. C is a stepped wall in plan, both planes dashed. Colours as in Table 9.10.2.1.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.10.14.2. (page 9-80), with definitions from Division A 1.4.1.2.
